column1: # This window as a caller: a name, a value.
# `name`: how the name it gives itself on a line begins; letters and
# digits chosen by chance follow. A browser's page names itself with
# digits and the letters a to f, and of two callers the one with the
# lesser name gives way when both offer at once: a name that begins
# after f never gives way to a browser.
# `pace`: how often it looks at what the line and its connections
# `wait`: how long it waits for the line to answer, in milliseconds.
# What it sends: sound at this many samples a second, on this many
# channels, a piece every this many milliseconds; and a picture this
# wide and high, this many a second.
# The sound it sends when it has no microphone: a tone of this many
# cycles a second, this share of full.
# How long a level it shows is taken over, in milliseconds.
# What carries a call when the real library is built in, as a person
# reads it; what the sound and the picture it sends are called, and
# The names in a server the line gives, as a browser reads them.
# Where the sound and the pictures of a call come from. `system`: the
# system's own microphone, camera and screen, and what arrives is
# played on its sound out. `stand`: the tone above and a grey ramp,
# and nothing is played. One run is given the other with
# `--set device=stand`: the tests and every picture in doc/ are made
# so, and nothing of a person's room or screen is ever kept.
# A screen that is shared: the stream it is sent under, so the other
# end can tell it from a camera, and what its picture is called; which
# of the system's screens, counted from 0; how many pictures of it a
# second; how wide the copy this window shows of it is at most; how
# wide and high the stand-in's is; and how many pictures it asks the
# system for before it gives up on a first.
# What is heard: the share of full it is played at, and the most that
# is kept waiting to be played, in milliseconds.
# How long no picture comes under a stream before it counts as over,
# in milliseconds: a camera turned off says nothing.
# What the pictures of a call are named in the window's film: how the
# names begin, and whose this window's own are.
# The names of what the system may not give: the text table says each
# Why, where the system said nothing itself: it has no such device;
# and the library could make nothing that takes pictures of a screen.

column2: nothing here can take a picture of a screen
